Does “right shift operation any number of times” allow zero shifts, i.e., is the original array considered a valid result?
Must the sorted target be strictly non‑decreasing (allowing equal elements) or strictly increasing?
If the array contains duplicate values, how should ties be handled when determining if the array can be sorted by shifts?
Are there any constraints on the type of elements (e.g., integers only, comparable objects) that the function must accept?
Should the function treat an array with a single element as trivially sortable (return True) even without shifting?
Is the function expected to modify the input list in place or leave it unchanged?
For an empty array, should the function return True without performing any checks, or should it also handle None or other falsy inputs?
